messages:
katie: quick question — we're onboarding a hosted monitoring collector (monitorly.example.com). The vendor only supports collector IP ranges (no PrivateLink). For our new dedicated VPC should we: (A) add their CIDR(s) to the NAT egress allowlist, or (B) set up a dedicated bastion to proxy? Also: any logging redaction rules we should apply for outbound connections? :thinking:

sam: my vote is NAT egress allowlist + strict security group + explicit ticket/justification. spinning up a bastion adds ops burden and doesn't reduce network exposure much if outbound is allowed anyway. :+1:

katie: noted. vendor sent these ranges: `203.0.113.0/28` and `198.51.100.64/27`. Is it acceptable to put those on the nat gateway egress rule for the dedicated subnet?

lisa: two quick things on logging: 1) don't log full request URLs or query params from the collector, only log status/latency + hashed path if you need to correlate. 2) strip any container/env metadata that could contain secrets (ENV_*, AWS creds). We normally use the scrub rule `s/(token|password|secret)=[^&\s]+/REDACTED/gi` in the log pipeline.

sam: also add a short justification in the ticket: business owner, data classification (PII/no), retention needs. Security will require retention <= 90 days for external collectors unless approved.

katie: they said they don't store PII and only collect aggregated metrics, but they can accept a Data Processing Addendum. I'll attach.

security-engineering note from dave: prefer limiting at the subnet NAT ACL or SG level where possible. If you must add to the NAT, scope to the minimum ports (443) and CIDRs. Example SG egress snippet we use: ```
- Type: egress
  Protocol: TCP
  PortRange: 443
  Destination: 203.0.113.0/28
  Description: monitoring-collector
```

katie: thanks — should I include both CIDRs on the same rule or separate rules per CIDR?

dave: separate rules per CIDR is easier to audit and revoke individually. Tag rules with `owner:katie` and `purpose:monitoring-collector` in the ticket.

audit-bot: FYI security policy SC-NET-03 requires a change ticket and a review before any external CIDR is added to prod NAT allowlists. Link your ticket here and @eng-security will review.

lisa: on redaction again — avoid logging container IDs if possible; we prefer an internal trace id only. If you need to map, store mapping in a locked internal DB with limited access.

katie: got it. I'll open a change request with justification, the vendor DPA, CIDRs separated, ports limited to 443, and add log-scrub config per Lisa. Will ping when ticket is up. :thumbsup:

sam: sounds good, thanks Katie. :eyes:
